claims.text: Controlled aluminization can create a continuous, adherent Al2O3 surface layer on a refractory high-entropy alloy.
A continuous, adherent Al2O3 surface layer will improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy lacks an engineered protective oxide scale.
Pack-cementation aluminization enriches the alloy surface with aluminum.
The aluminum-enriched surface forms a dense Al2O3 layer during high-temperature exposure.
The treatment produces a uniform, continuous, and adherent Al2O3 scale on the alloy surface.
Aluminization promotes selective oxidation of aluminum at the enriched surface.
The resulting alumina layer acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Reduced oxygen diffusion through the alumina layer slows oxidation of the underlying alloy.
After approximately 100 hours at 1200°C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere, the aluminized alloy will have a lower oxidation rate than the untreated alloy.
The aluminized alloy will exhibit lower mass gain than the untreated alloy after the specified exposure.
The aluminized alloy will exhibit a thinner and more protective oxide scale than the untreated alloy after the specified exposure.
The magnitude of the oxidation improvement may depend on aluminization processing details and the intrinsic alloy composition.
